summary:
Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires stands under Argentina's national framework for legal gender recognition, health care and hate-crime law. The sources identify two region-anchored findings for the city and no city-specific statute or enforcement statistic.

Trans activists based in Buenos Aires told the Washington Blade, in reporting published on 10 April 2025, that police violence against trans and travesti sex workers has become more common since the current national government took office. The same account records harassment and hate speech rising nationally.

DNU 61/2025, one of two emergency decrees published in February 2025, re-regulates the housing of transgender people deprived of liberty and invites the provinces and the City of Buenos Aires to adhere. The decree bars people who have legally changed gender from being housed in women's prisons when they are detained for sexual offences or violence against women. Whether the City of Buenos Aires has adhered is not stated in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The city hosts trans activist organisations named for Diana Sacayán and for Lohana Berkins, and figures from those organisations were among the Buenos Aires-based sources for the April 2025 reporting on police violence against trans and travesti sex workers.

The source does not state whether the reported increase in police violence is confined to the city or reflects a wider national trend; the national hate-crime and security-force figures are carried by Argentina's national record.
localsOnly:
For residents, the operative question in the available sources is the city's response to DNU 61/2025: adherence would extend to local custody the rule barring people who have legally changed gender from women's prisons when detained for sexual offences or violence against women. The sources do not record whether the City of Buenos Aires has adhered.

Trans sex workers in the city are the group named in the April 2025 reporting on increased police violence; no city-specific count or complaint mechanism is given.
outOfScopeNotes:
No city-specific statute, ordinance or enforcement statistic for Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires appears in the source inventory; the region-anchored findings are the reported police violence and the invitation to adhere to DNU 61/2025.

Whether the City of Buenos Aires has adhered to DNU 61/2025 is unresolved in the sources.

Whether the reported increase in police violence against trans and travesti sex workers is specific to the city or national in scope is not resolved by the source.
